key_agent_trends: EU Commission opens €297 million Horizon Europe calls for frontier AI, robotics and energy-efficient data centres to boost tech sovereignty.
Irish-founded Hoplite raises $5.5 million from Stripe founders for cloud platform running swarms of AI coding agents.
Deutsche Telekom's T.Capital invests €100 million in Mistral AI to advance sovereign European AI for German industry.
OVHcloud unveils Olala family of sovereign LLMs and AI agent tools at its Paris summit, trained on European supercomputers.
Commission adopts Implementing Regulation setting common rules for AI regulatory sandboxes across the EU, prioritising SMEs.

stories.headline: European Commission opens €297 million Horizon Europe calls for AI, robotics and sustainable data centres
stories.what_happened: On 17 November 2026 the European Commission opened two Horizon Europe calls totalling €297 million under the Digital, Industry and Space work programme. €107 million targets frontier AI with safety by design, AI-enabled robotics and sectoral uptake; €112 million supports energy-efficient AI data processing and data centres; remaining funds cover photonics, virtual worlds and standardisation. Proposals are due by 18 March 2027.
stories.why_it_matters: The funding aims to close Europe's innovation gap, reduce external dependencies and support trustworthy AI development and deployment aligned with EU priorities.

stories.headline: Irish-founded Hoplite raises $5.5 million from Stripe founders for cloud AI coding agent swarms
stories.what_happened: On or around 20 November 2026 Hoplite, founded by Irish University of Limerick dropouts Ryan Morrissey and Bence Redmond and based in Dublin and San Francisco, raised $5.5 million. The round was led by Stripe co-founders John and Patrick Collison, with participation from Y Combinator, Paul Graham, Des Traynor and others. The platform lets developers run multiple AI coding agents in the cloud rather than on local machines.
stories.why_it_matters: It lowers the infrastructure barrier for agentic software development, enabling small teams to scale coding agents without managing local environments or keeping laptops online.

stories.headline: Deutsche Telekom's T.Capital invests €100 million in Mistral AI for sovereign AI in Germany
stories.what_happened: On 19 November 2026 Deutsche Telekom announced that its T.Capital Tech Fund invested €100 million in Mistral AI's Series D. The move is a first step toward a strategic partnership combining Telekom's infrastructure and integration with Mistral's models to support German enterprises and public institutions, particularly in industrial and regulated sectors. Mistral has a Munich hub.
stories.why_it_matters: It strengthens European sovereign AI options by pairing a major telecom's trusted infrastructure with a leading European model provider for enterprise deployment.

stories.headline: OVHcloud unveils Olala sovereign LLM family at AI Summit, including CPU-runnable mini model
stories.what_happened: On 19 November 2026 at its AI Summit in Paris, OVHcloud unveiled the Olala family of large language models developed via its OVHai LLM subsidiary (from Dragon LLM research). Olala mini (about 7B parameters, 1B active) was trained on European public supercomputers, runs on a single CPU server, and is already used by Qwant for instant answers. The company also launched AI agent hosting tools and expanded GPU capacity.
stories.why_it_matters: It advances European sovereign AI by providing open, efficient models and full-stack infrastructure that keep data and control within Europe.

stories.headline: European Commission adopts Implementing Regulation setting common rules for AI regulatory sandboxes
stories.what_happened: On 10 November 2026 the European Commission adopted Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/2487, published 11 November, laying down detailed rules for the establishment, operation and supervision of AI regulatory sandboxes under the AI Act. It provides priority and free access for SMEs and startups, requires Member States to have national sandboxes by 2 August 2027, and enters into force on 1 December 2026. Exit reports are mutually recognisable.
stories.why_it_matters: Common rules reduce fragmentation, support innovation especially for smaller firms, and create a consistent framework for testing AI systems under regulatory supervision before market placement.
